_why: ADR 0197's mutation table, re-derived under scripts/mutate.py.
ADR 0197 adds a check that says which LLM providers actually work. The
mutations target the distinctions that make it worth running rather than
the request itself.
D1 judges a provider on HTTP status alone. That is the SiliconFlow
failure: 200 with an error body saying the balance is empty. A checker
that trusts the status reports an unusable provider as healthy, which is
worse than not checking.
D2 collapses `unconfigured` into `broken`, so a provider nobody set up
reads as one that is failing, and an operator debugs a provider they
never intended to use.
D3 returns exit 0 when nothing is configured. Zero failures over zero
providers is the same shape of lie as an empty test suite passing.
D4 removes the finish_reason 'length' allowance, restoring the false
positive the first version of this file produced: a reasoning model that
spends its token budget thinking was reported BROKEN while working
perfectly. It is here because a check that condemns something working is
worse than no check -- somebody acts on it.
Not included, because no test here catches it: whether `explain`'s
substring matching classifies a provider message it has never seen. It
matches on words like 'balance' and 'does not exist'; a vendor phrasing
the same refusal differently falls through to the raw HTTP line, which
is honest but unhelpful, and nothing tests that path.
Run:  python3 scripts/mutate.py --set docs/mutations/adr-0197-llm-doctor.json

mutations.description: a 200 response is accepted without reading the body
mutations._note: The SiliconFlow shape: HTTP 200, error in the body. Judging on status alone reports a provider that refuses every request as healthy -- and since Terrium falls back to keyword classification silently, nothing downstream would contradict it.

mutations.description: a provider with no key is reported as broken
mutations._note: Absence is not a fault. Collapsing the two sends an operator to debug a provider they never intended to use, and buries the ones that are genuinely broken in a list of five.

mutations.description: no providers configured exits 0 instead of 3
mutations._note: Zero failures over zero providers reads as a clean bill of health. Same shape as an empty test suite passing: the check ran, found nothing wrong, and checked nothing.

mutations.description: a reasoning model that used its token budget is called broken
mutations._note: The false positive this file shipped with for one run. Groq's openai/gpt-oss-120b returned finish_reason 'length' with empty content because the probe asked for 8 tokens; the key authenticated, the model existed and tokens were generated. Condemning a working provider is worse than not checking, because the report is acted on.
